items.title: Biogen shifts M&A strategy as Apellis acquisition pushes revenue above analyst expectations
items.snippet: Biogen officially began reporting revenue from the $5.6 billion acquisition of Apellis in the second quarter, shaking up analysts’ consensus estimates and leading to a beat.

items.title: Kyverna taps ElevateBio to secure commercial supply of autoimmune CAR-T therapy
items.snippet: ElevateBio will be the primary source of Kyverna’s autologous CAR-T cell therapy for anticipated U.S. and global launches in autoimmune indications.

items.title: Do you need oncology experience to land an oncology job?
items.snippet: Business stage is just one factor in whether biopharmas want job candidates to have oncology experience for oncology roles. Two recruiters explain when oncology expertise matters most, the mistakes job seekers make and how to make a good impression.

items.title: 7 companies hiring in New York now
items.snippet: Looking for a biopharma job in New York? Check out the BioSpace list of seven companies hiring life sciences professionals like you.

items.title: Incyte cuts early-stage cancer drug to focus on next-gen programs
items.snippet: Investors are focused on Incyte’s late-stage programs as the biotech braces for the 2028 patent cliff of its leading product Jakafi.

items.title: Novo ordered to face CagriSema fraud claims from shareholders: New Jersey court
items.snippet: Shareholders allege that Novo Nordisk withheld information about crucial protocol changes in a Phase 3 study of the weight loss drug CagriSema, which led investors to buy company shares “at artificially inflated prices.”

items.title: GSK cost-cutting plan includes global layoffs
items.snippet: Follow along as BioSpace tracks job cuts and restructuring initiatives.

items.title: 2026 IPO stock tracker: How newly public biotechs are performing
items.snippet: BioSpace is launching an IPO dashboard to help the industry keep tabs on U.S. biotechs that have taken the public plunge in 2026.

items.title: Capricor and Replimune prep for FDA adcomms, Q2 earnings roll on, Sarepta’s new leader, more
items.snippet: The FDA published briefing documents ahead of advisory committee meetings for therapies from Capricor Therapeutics and Replimune indicate an uphill battle for the biotechs; GSK and AstraZeneca outline ambitious plans in second quarter presentations; Sarepta taps Michael Severino as its new CEO; and Amgen launches its...

items.title: Biotechs bring big launches and pharma rivalries into Q2 earnings period
items.snippet: With the second quarter earnings period underway, BioSpace examines five biotechs with meaningful catalysts that analysts and investors are watching.

items.title: Webinar: Building the Intelligence Engine for Drug Discovery R&D Teams
items.snippet: Drug discovery teams have more data than ever, but turning that data into actionable insight remains a major challenge. In this candid conversation, Patsnap’s Ben Coverdale is joined by Mark Davies, Head of Product for Life Sciences, and James Longden, Senior Director, Life Sciences at Evolvus to explore how AI-powere...

items.title: GSK shares rise as $2.5B cost-cutting plan unveiled
items.snippet: As GSK records $2.4 billion in impairment charges for the second quarter, the U.K. pharma has announced a sweeping restructure designed to save about the same amount of money over the next few years.

items.title: FDA says Replimune’s melanoma data package is ‘not interpretable,’ setting up tough adcomm
items.snippet: The FDA's rebuff of Replimune comes a day after the agency similarly called into question the Phase 3 trial for Capricor’s Duchenne muscular dystrophy cell therapy.

items.title: Altimmune rises as GLP-1/glucagon drug curbs heavy drinking in mid-stage study
items.snippet: Pemvidutide showed a “highly statistically significant” treatment effect in patients with alcohol use disorder. Altimmune is going up against Eli Lilly and newcomer Baseline Therapeutics, among others, in this space.

items.title: Apnimed eyes up to $160M IPO to prep for sleep apnea drug launch
items.snippet: If the offering closes, Apnimed will join the 2026 IPO class that has already far surpassed last year’s total.

items.title: Oak Hill takes SPAC track to Nasdaq with Roche asset in tow
items.snippet: Oak Hill Bio is developing the antisense therapy rugonersen, which it licensed from Roche in 2025, for Angelman syndrome.

items.title: As pharma descends on China for deals, BIOSECURE Act raises intellectual property risk
items.snippet: When signing a biotech licensing deal in China, experts say that pharma’s patent attorneys need to understand the geopolitical risk of the BIOSECURE Act.

items.title: UPDATE: FDA disputes Capricor's claims of Phase 3 success for DMD cell therapy
items.snippet: In briefing documents published Monday ahead of an advisory committee meeting for deramiocel, the FDA disagreed with Capricor's assertion that a Phase 3 trial met its primary outcome measures.

items.title: MapLight’s schizophrenia pill remains in Cobenfy’s shadow after mixed Phase 2 readout
items.snippet: While MapLight Therapeutics’ oral schizophrenia candidate reached the main endpoint of a Phase 2 trial, analysts say Bristol Myers Squibb's Cobenfy is likely to hold its market share.

items.title: Gossamer regains rights to lung disease asset from Chiesi after Phase 3 fail
items.snippet: Despite a Phase 3 miss, Gossamer Bio is full steam ahead for its lung disease asset, pointing to previous “review issues” at the FDA as one of the reasons to continue development.

items.title: Biotech’s China problem: An issue of national security or economic value for the US?
items.snippet: Congressional letters sent to the CEOs of Eli Lilly, Pfizer, Merck, BMS and AbbVie this week voicing concerns about the pharmas' clinical trials in China highlight an ongoing discrepancy in how government and industry think about the rise of the Asian country’s biotech industry.

items.title: BIO 2026: Cell and gene therapy sector must break the mold to thrive
items.snippet: If cell and gene therapy makers are going to achieve their mission to improve patients’ lives, the industry must come together to share information across stakeholders, from regulators to manufacturers to payers.

items.title: At FDA, ‘caretaker mode’ is better than power trip mode
items.snippet: UniQure’s planned third-quarter submission for its Huntington’s disease gene therapy may be a harbinger of a more flexible FDA under acting commissioner Kyle Diamantas—but how long will it last? And how can companies be sure these positive decisions won’t just be reversed?

items.title: Lilly just bought renowned regulator Peter Marks a pipeline to play with
items.snippet: FDA veteran Peter Marks will now shape the future of Eli Lilly’s vaccines work after the buys of Curevo, LimmaTech Biologics and Vaccine Company for up to $3.8 billion total.
